title: Startup skeleton · round 1
build: python3 -I design/startup-skeleton-brief/inline-imports.py design/features/startup-skeleton design/language/source build/skel-boards, then build.mjs on build/skel-boards (the Timeline board imports Agents-Mate-1280, which the boards-page shim does not resolve)
intro: Claude Design, 22 Nov. Three directions for what a Mac window shows before the core is up; all three are client-only (a), no SDUI, plugin or core change.

A · Remembered layout (designer's pick): the window opens as it was last time. Rail icons, selected section and pane layout come from a small client cache (≈1 KB per window); each pane is drawn in the shape of its kind (list, transcript, detail, table; a terminal pane stays plain bg).
B · Neutral frame: no cache. Rail squares, default sidebar, one generic row shape in every pane. Simplest, but the layout jumps at ready when the sidebar was hidden or the chat column was shown.
C · Remembered geometry: caches only which panes show and their widths. No jump, but an anonymous rail and list rows over a terminal; same cache mechanism as A for less.

For A: skeleton at 0 ms, no text; ≥ 5 s status bar 'Starting core…' with a mini progress; ≥ 15 s 'Still starting core…' + Show log ⌘L; ready → 180 ms cross-fade (none if ready ≤ 250 ms); failure → chrome stays, message + Retry ⌘R at the top of the content; reconnect → last content at full ink, core actions disabled. The designer moved the slow threshold from 3 s to 5 s because the test app is ready at 3.6 s.
